lead.headline: Netanyahu Edges Ahead in Israel's Election, but Neither Bloc Has a Majority
lead.summary: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing religious alliance was projected to win 53 seats in the 120-member Knesset on Wednesday afternoon, according to Bloomberg. Opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot's bloc was projected to win 48 seats, with almost 93% of votes counted. Both blocs fall short of the 61 seats needed to govern. The two Israeli Arab parties nearly doubled their projected total to 19 seats, which could make them kingmakers in coalition talks. Eisenkot had declared victory earlier in the day, when preliminary results showed his bloc slightly ahead. Turnout of about 77.7% was the highest in a Knesset election in 27 years, and Israeli bonds and the shekel fell because there was no clear winner.
lead.deck: With almost all votes counted, a surge in support for Arab parties has made them possible kingmakers and left the race to form a government wide open.

tech.headline: OpenAI Says Its Models Produced Proofs in Math, Computing and Physics
tech.summary: OpenAI says its internal models have produced new results that include a proof that Yang-Mills theory exists, which is one part of a Clay Millennium Prize problem. Anthropic has also announced proof results, and experts are now reviewing both companies' claims. The paper on the Yang-Mills problem has not yet been made public.

tech.headline: Start-Up's A.I. Agents Got Into Anthropic's Business Systems in Under 12 Hours
tech.summary: Cathedral, a cybersecurity start-up founded by former DOGE staffers, says its A.I. agents reached Anthropic's internal systems through flaws in third-party business software. Anthropic confirmed the researchers accessed a limited set of its sales, HR and IT systems. It said customer conversations with Claude, its source code and its model weights were not touched. The company also said Cathedral exaggerated the national security implications and did not fully follow the rules of its bug-bounty-style program.

tech.headline: SpaceX Secures $40 Billion GPU Financing Deal With Apollo
tech.summary: In a regulatory filing, SpaceX disclosed a binding commitment for about $40 billion in financing for A.I. chips and related data center equipment. Under the deal, an entity managed by Apollo Global Management will buy the hardware and lease it to SpaceX for about five years. SpaceX called it the largest committed GPU financing.

business.headline: SK Hynix Profit Jumps Sevenfold as A.I. Memory Demand Surges
business.summary: SK Hynix reported quarterly operating profit of 83.3 trillion won, beating analysts' estimates, on revenue of 104.6 trillion won. The memory chipmaker also announced an additional shareholder return program for 2026 worth 100 trillion won, or about $75 billion. The results come as A.I. infrastructure spending faces growing scrutiny.

business.headline: GE Vernova to Buy Grid Supplier Trench Group for $9 Billion
business.summary: GE Vernova agreed to acquire Trench Group to expand its range of high-voltage power grid equipment as demand for electricity rises. The deal will be paid for equally with cash and debt and is expected to close in late 2027. The company also raised its sales guidance, saying its customer backlog had grown to $197 billion.

business.headline: Oil Rises After Attack on Saudi Refinery Revives Supply Fears
business.summary: Oil prices rose more than 1% on Wednesday after Yemen's Houthis said they had struck Saudi Arabia's largest refinery. The gain followed a drop of nearly $2 on Tuesday. ING strategists said the market was still pricing in a greater chance of renewed escalation in the region.

world.headline: U.S. Tells Gulf Allies to Prepare for Possible Iran Strikes After Midterms
world.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported that the U.S. has told several Gulf countries it may carry out a short, intense military operation against Iran after the midterm elections. President Trump has not made a final decision, but U.S. forces in the region have been preparing for possible strikes. The White House declined to comment on what it called sensitive military plans.

world.headline: Houthis Say They Hit Saudi Arabia's Largest Oil Refinery
world.summary: Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis said on Tuesday they had struck Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery with a ballistic missile, causing a fire. Saudi authorities did not immediately confirm the strike. The Houthis also said they had repelled an advance by Saudi-backed forces near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.

world.headline: Flávio Bolsonaro Flees to U.S. After Losing Brazil's Election
world.summary: Flávio Bolsonaro has arrived in the United States after losing Sunday's presidential runoff to President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. CNN Brasil reported that Brazil's Federal Police had canceled his passports after he failed to surrender them. He had initially refused to concede, saying his team would ask for the results to be annulled.

opinion.headline: Anthropic Is Bringing the 'Anti-Sell' Strategy to Its IPO
opinion.summary: Lee argues that Anthropic's IPO prospectus works like the 'anti-sell' pitch the company uses with job candidates. In his view, it is a deliberately sobering, doomsday-style document meant to weed out investors who may not be able to stomach the risks ahead.
opinion.author: Dave Lee

opinion.headline: For Russia, Trump's Diesel Deal Was Just the First Ask
opinion.summary: The Atlantic Council piece argues that Trump's diesel deal with Moscow is politically convenient before the midterms but will not meaningfully lower U.S. pump prices or noticeably reduce Russia's budget deficit. It presents Moscow's request to lift sanctions on the Russian Direct Investment Fund as a follow-on demand.
opinion.author: Atlantic Council

sports.headline: Rays Walk Off Brewers 4-3 in 12 Innings to Avoid World Series Sweep
sports.summary: Ben Williamson's walk-off in the 12th inning gave the Tampa Bay Rays a 4-3 win over the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 4 of the World Series. Earlier, Jonny DeLuca's RBI single had tied the game. Milwaukee still leads the series 3-1, and Game 5 is Wednesday night.

sports.headline: Fourth-Tier Fleetwood Knocks Arsenal Out of Carabao Cup
sports.summary: Premier League champion Arsenal lost to League Two side Fleetwood Town on penalties in the Carabao Cup fourth round on Tuesday. Fleetwood goalkeeper Jay Lynch saved Bruno Guimarães's spot kick before teenage defender Conor Haughey scored the winning penalty. Earlier, the match had been halted for about eight minutes after a drone was spotted over the ground.

sports.headline: Towns Leads Knicks Past Unbeaten Pistons 111-97 for First Win
sports.summary: Karl-Anthony Towns had 27 points and 20 rebounds as the New York Knicks beat the previously unbeaten Detroit Pistons 111-97 on Tuesday. The win kept the defending champion Knicks from falling to 0-4. It would have been only the second 0-4 start by a defending champion in NBA history.
